# Results — Study 796 (Corporate-Bond-Low-Risk)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
the **low-risk / betting-against-beta anomaly** (Frazzini & Pedersen 2014): the safest
assets earn the highest *risk-adjusted* returns, so a portfolio that levers up the safe
leg and de-levers the risky leg earns a premium. We test the bond-ETF version by ranking
on trailing volatility. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `1f2efa58efab` (11-name total-return panel,
identical tape to Study 795).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return (auto-adjusted close) for an 11-name credit + Treasury bond-ETF basket, 4,903 rows, 2007-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Universe | low-risk pole: SHY, VCSH · mid: LQD, IEF, BKLN · high-risk pole: VCLT, TLT, HYG, JNK, ANGL, EMB |
| Risk proxy | trailing **1-year (252-day) daily-return volatility**, annualised, at each month-end (63d / 126d as robustness) |
| Portfolio | rank on vol; long the **bottom third** (low-vol), short the **top third** (high-vol); each leg **scaled to a common ex-ante 6%/yr risk** (avg leverage low **2.59x** / high **0.76x**), rebalanced monthly |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag — form on the month-*t* close, earn month *t+1* (one `shift`); one-way turnover × cost × NAV; a single financing/borrow rate on the borrowed notional (levered-long above 1x plus the short leg), pro-rated monthly |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (auto-adjusted close) throughout — coupons folded in, both legs on the same convention |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is credit/Treasury ETFs still
trading in 2026, chosen ex post and projected backwards. For the BAB direction the bias is
subtle: a survivor set that dropped blown-up high-vol vehicles would *understate* the risky
leg's drawdowns and thus *understate* the low-risk premium — so the null we find is not
manufactured *by* the bias.

## The claim's plain form — Sharpe of low-vol vs high-vol (unlevered baskets)

| basket | mean/yr | vol/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **low-vol** (bottom third) | +2.59% | 3.53% | **0.74** | +3.36 |
| **high-vol** (top third) | +6.61% | 10.54% | **0.63** | +2.67 |

The low-vol basket does earn a slightly higher Sharpe (0.74 vs 0.63) — directionally what
the anomaly predicts. But the gap is a whisker, and both HAC *t*'s just say "bonds went up".
The real test is whether a *risk-matched spread* can bank that whisker.

## The headline — vol-scaled low-minus-high (BAB), 1-year vol sort, hold 1 month

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| months held (n) | 217 |
| BAB mean (annualised) | **+0.84%/yr** |
| BAB vol (annualised) | 6.25%/yr |
| Sharpe (gross) | **0.13** |
| **HAC (Newey-West) *t*** | **+0.51** (plain *t* = +0.57) |
| hit rate (BAB month > 0) | 59.4% (Wilson 95% [52.8%, 65.8%]) |
| max drawdown / worst month | −26.0% / −14.78% |
| avg leverage (low / high leg) | 2.59x / 0.76x |
| avg one-way turnover | 24.2% / month |
| turnover break-even (one-way) | 28.9 bps |

The risk-matched spread earns a small positive drift, **nowhere near significance**: HAC
*t* = +0.51. It is positive in 59.4% of months (Wilson excludes 50%) yet the *mean* is dead —
the signature of a negatively-skewed leverage book: many small wins, rare big losses (worst
month −14.78%, −26% drawdown). **Vol-rank-shuffle placebo:** the real spread (+1.29%/yr under
the placebo's fast per-asset-mean-vol leg-scaling proxy — hence slightly above the leg-basket-vol
book headline of +0.84%/yr) sits against a placebo mean of **+4.87%/yr** (sd 1.58) over 2,000
permutations of the monthly volatility assignment → **p = 0.989**. A *random* ranking earns
*more* than the real low-vol ranking: the spread's return is a leverage artifact, not a
low-risk signal.

## Robustness — the vol-estimation window

| trailing-vol window | mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 63d (~3m) | +1.07% | 0.14 | +0.55 | 220 |
| 126d (~6m) | +0.05% | 0.01 | +0.03 | 218 |
| **252d (~1y, headline)** | **+0.84%** | 0.13 | **+0.51** | 217 |

Flat at every window — no vol-estimation horizon rescues it.

## Myth-check — is it just the 2022 duration crash?

| sample | mean/yr | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| full | +0.84% | +0.51 | 217 |
| ex-2022 | +1.10% | +0.64 | 205 |

In 2022, long-duration TLT collapsed and the low-vol (short-duration) leg would have shone —
but dropping 2022 leaves the spread *just as flat* (if anything marginally stronger). This is
not a duration-crash artifact; it is simply not real in either sub-sample.

## Subperiods — sign-unstable, never significant

| era | mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2008-2015 | −1.38% | −0.24 | −0.73 | 92 |
| 2016-2026 | +2.47% | 0.38 | +1.01 | 125 |

Negative in the first half, faintly positive in the second, neither clearing *t* = 1. There
is no era where the ETF-panel low-risk spread is real.

## The timer — net of realistic costs, financing on the leverage

Turnover break-even ≈ **28.9 bps** one-way (gross +7.0 bps/month against 24.2% monthly
turnover) — but that ignores the financing on the ~2.6x-levered safe leg. Charging it:

| one-way cost | financing/borrow | net mean/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | 50 bps/yr | **−0.48%** | −0.08 | −0.29 |
| 10 bps | 75 bps/yr | **−1.21%** | −0.19 | −0.74 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps/yr | **−2.09%** | −0.33 | −1.27 |

The gross edge was never significant, and financing the leverage pushes the net *negative*
everywhere. There is no residual to trade.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic total-return panel with a TUNABLE planted low-risk tilt (seed 314): each asset's
Sharpe is tilted inversely to its volatility, so the low-vol names earn more per unit of risk.
At strength 0 every asset sits on one Sharpe line (the null); no network.

| planted lowrisk_strength | BAB mean/yr | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −0.2% | **−0.08** |
| 0.30 | +3.0% | +1.27 |
| 0.60 | +6.3% | +2.63 |
| 1.00 | +10.5% | **+4.44** |

Null over **20 seeds**: mean HAC *t* = **+0.17**, **|t| > 2 in 1/20 seeds** (≈ the 5% you'd
expect by chance). The detector is unbiased and has ample power — it recovers a planted
low-risk premium cleanly, so the flat real-tape *t* = +0.51 is a true reading of the ETF panel,
not a broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The risk-matched low-minus-high bond-ETF spread earns +0.84%/yr at **HAC
  *t* = +0.51** — insignificant — with a vol-rank-shuffle placebo **p = 0.989** (a random
  ranking earns *more*), flat across vol-windows and the 2022 cut, and sign-unstable across
  eras. The low-vol basket's Sharpe edge (0.74 vs 0.63) is a whisker that does not survive the
  trade. This bond-ETF panel shows no betting-against-beta premium.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Turnover break-even ≈ 29 bps, but the safe leg is levered ~2.6x, so
  financing pushes the net **negative** at every realistic cost (−0.5% at 5 bps to −2.1% at
  20 bps). Gross Sharpe 0.13, a −26% drawdown, a single −14.8% month. There is no edge to charge
  costs against.
- **Ranked on real volatility? — NOT SUPPORTED.** A random vol-ranking earns +4.87%/yr vs the
  real +1.29%/yr — the spread's return is a leverage artifact, not a low-risk signal. Consistent
  with the betting-against-beta effect living in the single-name cross-section that a coarse,
  IG-and-Treasury-heavy ETF panel cannot reproduce.
